To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the T lymphocyte-deprived mice were not able to control a systemic BCG infection.

T lymphocyte-deprived mice develop systemic BCG infections which are lethal, that these mice do not develop hypersensitivity, and that the infected mice develop lung lesions which are similar to those seen in normal mice but which are not associated with a regression of the granulomas.
T cell-depleted mice infected with BCG die of the infection and that these mice fail to develop antitubercle immune responses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the immunological and pathological events which occur during BCG infection of normal and immunologically deficient mice.
the role of the T lymphocyte in the induction of immunity to tuberculosis.
the role of T and B lymphocytes in the host response to BCG infection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
T lymphocytes are essential to the induction of antituberculotic immunity in BCG-infeceted mice, and that this immunity is not dependent upon the development of tuberculin sensitivity.
T lymphocytes are necessary for the development of antinocobacterial immunity and the development of granulomas.
the immune system plays a major part in controlling the BCG infection in the normal animal.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BCG-infected T lymphocyte-deficient mice develop a progressive infection which is associated with the appearance of macroscopic lung lesions.
the development of antinuberculous immunity is T lymphocyte dependent.
the T cell is essential for the development of antinycobacterial immunity and that it is the major factor in the regression of BCG infection in the lung.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T cell is required for the development of the early immune response to BCG in mice.
T lymphocytes are required for a normal immune response to BCG.
the BCG-infected thymectomised, irradiated, bone marrow reconstituted mice (THxB) developed systemic infection which was fatal to 95% of these animals within 60-90 days.
